tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Peptide design and key physicochemical parameters.
footnotes: a Molecular weight (MW) was measured by mass spectroscopy (MS); b The hydrophobic moment (μH) of a peptide is its hydrophobic moment relative to that of a perfectly amphipathic peptide. This yields a better measure of peptide amphipathicity using different scales; c The mean hydrophobicity (H) is the total hydrophobicity (sum of all residue hydrophobicity indices) divided by the number of residues.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Antimicrobial and hemolytic activities of the peptides.
footnotes: The final concentrations of peptides ranged from 0 μM to 256 μM. a Minimum inhibitory concentrations (MIC) are defined as the lowest concentration of peptide that inhibits bacterial growth; b Minimum hemolytic concentration (MHC) is the lowest concentration of peptide that causes 5% hemolysis of human red blood cells (hRBCs); c GM denotes the geometric mean of MIC values from all microbial strains in this table; d Therapeutic index (TI) is the ratio of the MHC to the geometric mean of all MICs. Larger values indicate greater cell selectivity.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: MIC values of antimicrobial peptides in the presence of physiological salts.
footnotes: The concentrations of salts were 150 mM NaCl, 4.5 mM KCl, 6 μM NH4Cl, 1 mM MgCl2, 1 mM MgCl2, 8 mM ZnCl3, 2.5 mM CaCl2 and 4 mM FeCl3.

footnotes: The final concentrations of peptides ranged from 0 μM to 256 μM.
